races.title: State Senate, District 36
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Tony Strickland
cands.bio: Republican state senator for District 36 since 2025. Earlier served in the Assembly (1998–2004) and the Senate for District 19 (2008–2012). Huntington Beach councilmember since 2022 and mayor 2022–2023. Whittier College political science graduate, former legislative staffer, runs a consulting firm and the Strong America super PAC.

controversies.text: In 2016 Strickland agreed to a $40,000 penalty from California's ethics commission. It found $65,000 in 2010 controller-race donations were routed through two county Republican committees, hiding the true donors, and his campaign filed false reports. Earlier fines: $6,000 for failing to report over $116,000 in late 1999 contributions, and $3,000 over an undisclosed mailer source.

In 2008 critics said Strickland's Senate campaign literature misrepresented his business background by listing him as a vice president of Green Wave Energy Solutions, which they said had not done business in California. A June 2008 release from his campaign called GreenWave a local energy company and named him its vice president. His response to the critics was not found.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed among his 2026 endorsements)

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from Strickland on data centers, restrictions on corporate or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His individual council votes on Huntington Beach housing matters were not in the pages we had. His claims about bills such as SB 296, SB 94, SB 710, SB 885 and SB 1015 come from his campaign site and were not checked against legislative records. The sponsored-legislation list on his Ballotpedia page was empty. Where Ballotpedia and Wikipedia do not say where he was raised, we relied on the 1973 family move to Ventura County.

local.label: Roots 100: He was born at Fort Ord, California, his family moved to Ventura County in 1973, and he has held office and lived in California since, including Huntington Beach.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember 1998–2004, state senator 2008–2012 and again from 2025, Huntington Beach councilmember and mayor from 2022, legislative staffer for Assemblyman Tom McClintock 1996–97, and a political and business consultant.
qual.why: He has served in both houses of the Legislature and in local elected office, and has worked in policy-related roles. Committee seats were not counted.
qual.label: He has served in both houses of the Legislature and in local elected office, and has worked in policy-related roles. Committee seats were not counted.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site says he has protected Proposition 13's cap on property taxes and helped reduce property taxes for disabled veterans (SB 296). It also cites a lifetime 'A' rating from the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association. These are campaign claims, and he does not say he would eliminate homestead taxes.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he has been a leading voice for fully funding Proposition 36 and works with Orange County Sheriff Don Barnes on a bill against online extortion of children (SB 1015). It also says police, firefighters and deputies support him.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: As a Huntington Beach councilmember and mayor he opposed increasing housing supply; during his tenure the city stopped accepting accessory dwelling unit applications, and Attorney General Rob Bonta sued the city. The page does not give his individual votes.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 1 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: He was born at Fort Ord, California, his family moved to Ventura County in 1973, and he has held office and lived in California since, including Huntington Beach.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Said Huntington Beach is '95% built out' and he will not support 'anything that guts our suburban coastal community.' In 2023 he said 'high rise high density urbanization' was being 'forced' on the city.

cands.name: Chris Duncan
cands.bio: Orange County attorney who focuses on tariffs and customs. Former federal prosecutor and senior attorney at U.S. Customs and Border Protection (DHS). San Clemente City Council member 2020–2024 and mayor 2022–2023. Ran unsuccessfully for State Assembly in 2020, 2022 and 2024.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists these endorsements for his 2026 campaign: the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Nurses Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, Equality California, Sierra Club Angeles Chapter, California Young Democrats, and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund. His own survey answer also lists SEIU, AFSCME, Attorney General Rob Bonta and several members of Congress.

cands.gaps: We found no record of any stance by Chris Duncan on data centers, homestead property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, school choice or teacher pay. His statements on housing are general: he supports expanding housing production with strong labor standards and cutting red tape. His claims about his record as mayor (reduced homelessness, beach funding, an offshore drilling ban resolution) come from his own campaign materials and were not independently confirmed. We could not confirm when he returned to California after studying in Massachusetts, Hawaii and Washington, D.C., or where he grew up beyond his own description. He has no state legislative record.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Oakland, CA, and in his 2024 candidate survey he calls himself a third-generation Californian and a graduate of California schools.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: About 16 years as a federal prosecutor and senior attorney at U.S. Customs and Border Protection and DHS, and a special assistant U.S. attorney. He holds a J.D. and an LL.M., is a business owner, and served on the San Clemente City Council from 2020 to 2024, including as mayor from 2022 to 2023.
qual.why: He has a law and policy career and local elected office, which fits the middle-to-upper range. He has not served in a state legislature or held chamber leadership.
qual.label: He has a law and policy career and local elected office, which fits the middle-to-upper range. He has not served in a state legislature or held chamber leadership.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he will fully fund police and support effective homeless solutions.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he will enforce tougher gun safety laws. His 2024 Ballotpedia survey likewise promised tougher gun safety laws.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he stands firm in supporting women's reproductive rights. In his 2024 survey he said he would stand up for access to safe, legal abortion and that he opposed a proposed abortion ban in his city.
